description: This classic Turkish Red Lentil Soup, known as Mercimek Corbasi, is a heartwarming and incredibly flavorful dish. Made with simple ingredients like red lentils, tomatoes, and aromatic spices, it's blended to a creamy perfection, offering comfort in every spoonful. It's a staple in Turkish homes, perfect as a starter or a light meal.

instructions.title: Prepare Lentils and Aromatics
instructions.text: Rinse the red lentils thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear. In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat a tablespoon of olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.

instructions.title: Sauté Garlic and Tomato Paste
instructions.text: Add the minced garlic to the pot and cook for another minute until fragrant. Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly, to deepen its flavor and color.

instructions.title: Add Spices and Lentils
instructions.text: Stir in the dried mint, red pepper flakes, and cumin. Cook for about 30 seconds until aromatic. Add the rinsed red lentils to the pot and stir to combine with the aromatics and spices.

instructions.title: Simmer the Soup
instructions.text: Pour in the vegetable or chicken broth (or water). Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are very tender and have broken down.

instructions.title: Blend to Perfection
instructions.text: Remove the pot from the heat. Using an immersion blender, blend the soup directly in the pot until smooth and creamy. Alternatively, carefully transfer the soup in batches to a regular blender and blend until smooth, then return to the pot. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.

instructions.title: Prepare the Chili Mint Butter Topping
instructions.text: In a small pan, melt the butter over medium-low heat. Once melted, add a pinch of red pepper flakes and a pinch of dried mint. Cook for 30 seconds until fragrant, being careful not to burn the butter. This will be drizzled over the soup.

instructions.title: Serve Mercimek Corbasi
instructions.text: Ladle the hot Mercimek Corbasi into serving bowls. Drizzle each serving with the prepared chili mint butter. Serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges on the side, allowing each person to squeeze lemon juice into their soup for an authentic Turkish flavor.

tips: For an extra smooth soup, pass it through a fine-mesh sieve after blending.
Adjust the amount of red pepper flakes (pul biber) to your preferred spice level. A good quality pul biber is key for authentic flavor.
Always serve Mercimek Corbasi with fresh lemon wedges; the acidity brightens the flavors beautifully.
article:
In the vast and varied tapestry of Turkish cuisine, few dishes evoke as much warmth and comfort as Mercimek Corbasi, the beloved Turkish Red Lentil Soup. This vibrant, creamy, and incredibly flavorful soup is a cornerstone of Turkish tables, enjoyed from bustling city restaurants to humble village homes. It's a dish that embodies simplicity, nutrition, and an unparalleled ability to soothe the soul. Whether you're seeking a hearty starter, a light lunch, or a nourishing meal on a chilly evening, Mercimek Corbasi delivers every time. Its vibrant color, delicate spices, and silky texture make it an irresistible culinary experience that's surprisingly easy to recreate in your own kitchen.

## What is Mercimek Corbasi (Turkish Red Lentil Soup)?

Mercimek Corbasi translates directly to "lentil soup," but it’s most famously known in its red lentil iteration. This classic Turkish Red Lentil Soup is characterized by its beautiful reddish-orange hue, smooth, creamy consistency, and subtly spiced flavor profile. Unlike some heartier lentil soups, Mercimek Corbasi is typically pureed until velvety smooth, offering a comforting warmth without being overly heavy. It's a staple across Turkey, often served with a generous squeeze of fresh lemon juice, which brightens its flavors, and a drizzle of *nane yağı*, a fragrant butter infused with dried mint and red pepper flakes.

More than just a soup, Mercimek Corbasi holds a special place in Turkish culture. It's a common sight at breakfast tables, a popular appetizer before main courses, and a go-to meal for those seeking something wholesome and easy to digest. Its high nutritional value, thanks to the protein-rich red lentils, makes it a fantastic vegetarian option. The simplicity of its ingredients belies the depth of flavor it achieves, making it a testament to the power of fresh, quality components handled with care.

## Ingredients for Turkish Red Lentil Soup

Creating an authentic Turkish Red Lentil Soup doesn't require an extensive list of exotic ingredients. In fact, most items are likely already in your pantry! Here's what you'll need:

*   **Red Lentils:** The star of the show. Ensure they are dried and rinsed thoroughly before cooking.
*   **Onion & Garlic:** The aromatic foundation that provides depth of flavor.
*   **Tomato Paste:** Adds a crucial umami note, a touch of sweetness, and contributes to the soup's signature color.
*   **Butter or Olive Oil:** Used for sautéing the aromatics and creating the flavorful *nane yağı* topping.
*   **Dried Mint (Nane):** Essential for the traditional topping, offering a refreshing and distinctive aroma.
*   **Red Pepper Flakes (Pul Biber):** Adds a mild heat and beautiful color to the mint butter. You can adjust the quantity to your spice preference.
*   **Paprika (Tatlı Pul Biber):** Sweet paprika adds a lovely color and mild flavor to the soup itself.
*   **Water or Vegetable Broth:** The liquid base for cooking the lentils. Broth will add more depth.
*   **Salt & Black Pepper:** To season the soup to perfection.
*   **Lemon Wedges:** Absolutely crucial for serving, providing a zesty counterpoint that elevates all the flavors.

## How to Make Mercimek Corbasi: Step-by-Step

Making this comforting Turkish Red Lentil Soup is a straightforward process that yields incredibly rewarding results.

1.  **Prepare the Lentils:** Start by thoroughly rinsing your red lentils under cold running water until the water runs clear. This removes any debris and excess starch, which can make the soup cloudy. Drain them well.
2.  **Sauté Aromatics:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, melt a tablespoon of butter or heat olive oil over medium heat. Add the finely chopped onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant, being careful not to burn it.
3.  **Build the Base:** Stir in the tomato paste, paprika, and a pinch of red pepper flakes (if using in the soup itself, otherwise save for the topping). Cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, to toast the spices and deepen the flavor of the tomato paste.
4.  **Add Lentils and Liquid:** Add the rinsed and drained red lentils to the pot. Pour in the water or vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until the lentils are completely soft and have broken down. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
5.  **Blend the Soup:** Remove the pot from the heat. Using an immersion blender, carefully blend the soup directly in the pot until it's completely smooth and creamy. If you don't have an immersion blender, carefully transfer the soup in batches to a regular blender (be cautious with hot liquids!) and blend until smooth. Return the blended soup to the pot.
6.  **Adjust Consistency and Seasoning:** If the soup is too thick, add a little more hot water or broth until it reaches your desired consistency. Season generously with salt and black pepper to taste. Gently reheat the soup over low heat, stirring occasionally.
7.  **Prepare the Mint Butter (Nane Yağı):** While the soup is reheating, prepare the traditional topping. In a small saucepan, melt a tablespoon or two of butter over medium-low heat. Once melted, stir in the dried mint and red pepper flakes. Cook for about 30 seconds to a minute, until fragrant, being careful not to burn the mint. The butter should turn a lovely reddish hue.
8.  **Serve:** Ladle the hot Mercimek Corbasi into bowls. Drizzle each serving with the fragrant mint butter and serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges on the side.

## Tips for the Best Turkish Red Lentil Soup

Achieving that perfect, restaurant-quality Turkish Red Lentil Soup is easy with a few simple tips:

*   **Rinse Those Lentils:** Don't skip this step! Rinsing removes starch and ensures a clearer, better-tasting soup.
*   **Quality Ingredients:** While simple, the quality of your tomato paste and butter makes a difference. A good, concentrated tomato paste will provide deeper flavor.
*   **Toast the Tomato Paste and Spices:** Cooking the tomato paste and spices briefly before adding liquid helps to deepen their flavor and remove any raw taste.
*   **Blend Thoroughly:** For that signature velvety texture, make sure you blend the soup until it's completely smooth. No grainy bits allowed!
*   **Don't Skimp on Lemon:** Lemon juice is not just a garnish; it's an essential flavor component that brightens the entire soup. Always serve with plenty of fresh lemon wedges.
*   **Taste and Adjust:** As with any soup, taste frequently during the cooking process and adjust salt, pepper, and even a touch more paprika if needed.
*   **Resting Time:** While you can serve it immediately, letting the soup rest for 10-15 minutes after blending allows the flavors to meld even further.

## Serving Suggestions for Mercimek Corbasi

Mercimek Corbasi is incredibly versatile and can be enjoyed in many ways. Here are some classic and delightful serving suggestions:

*   **The Classic Way:** Always serve with a generous drizzle of the *nane yağı* (mint and red pepper flake butter) and, most importantly, several fresh lemon wedges. A squeeze of lemon is non-negotiable for authentic flavor.
*   **With Bread:** Crusty Turkish bread (pide), a warm baguette, or even simple pita bread are perfect for dipping and soaking up every last drop of the delicious Turkish Red Lentil Soup.
*   **As an Appetizer:** It makes a wonderful start to any meal, especially a Turkish feast.
*   **Light Lunch or Dinner:** Paired with a simple green salad or some pickles, it creates a satisfying and nutritious light meal.
*   **Alongside Mezze:** Integrate it into a spread of Turkish appetizers for a truly authentic experience.

## Variations & Substitutions

While the classic Turkish Red Lentil Soup is perfect as is, there are a few ways you can customize it to your liking:

*   **Add Vegetables:** For extra nutrition and flavor, you can sauté finely diced carrots, potatoes, or bell peppers along with the onions and garlic. They will soften and blend beautifully into the soup.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of red pepper flakes in the soup base or the mint butter topping to make it as mild or spicy as you prefer.
*   **Herbs:** While dried mint is traditional for the topping, you can garnish with fresh parsley or cilantro for a different fresh note.
*   **Vegan Option:** Simply use olive oil instead of butter and ensure you use vegetable broth instead of water. The soup is naturally dairy-free otherwise.
*   **Thicker or Thinner:** Adjust the consistency by adding more water or broth if you prefer a thinner soup, or by simmering a little longer if you like it thicker.
*   **Smoked Paprika:** For a subtle smoky depth, substitute a portion of the sweet paprika with smoked paprika.

Mercimek Corbasi is more than just a soup; it's a hug in a bowl, a testament to the simple yet profound flavors of Turkish cuisine. Its ease of preparation, combined with its nutritional benefits and comforting taste, makes it a dish you'll want to return to again and again. So, gather your ingredients, follow these steps, and prepare to be enchanted by the timeless appeal of this incredible Turkish Red Lentil Soup. Enjoy!
